newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: 1,000 barrels Colombia crude spills into Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: 1,000 barrels Colombia crude spills into Venezuela.

text.p: At least 1,000 barrels of crude have spilled into rivers on either side of the Colombia-Venezuela border two weeks after a rebel dynamite attack on Colombia's main oil pipeline, authorities said Wednesday.

But a spokesman for Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol said the situation was under control and rejected Venezuelan media reports that the spillage could reach Lake Maracaibo and cause an environmental disaster.
"(Venezuelan oil company) Maraven is controlling the situation marvelously with detergents and floating barriers. Not a drop (of crude) will reach Lake Maracaibo," the Ecopetrol spokesman said.
"Certain groups in Venezuela are exaggerating this because it is a sensitive issue in terms of Colombian terrorist attacks," he added.

The 1,000 barrels that flowed along Colombia's River Sardinata and into Venezuela was just part of 8,800 barrels spilled after National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas blew up the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline in northeast Norte de Santander on June 15.
The crude was originally contained with the aid of floating barriers in the Quebrada Agua Linda, a tributary of the River Sardinata.
But heavy rains last weekend caused some of the crude to escape and flow across the border, the Ecopetrol spokesman said.
The pipeline runs from Occidental Petroleum Corp's field in Cano Limon in eastern Arauca province to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas.

The Cuban-inspired ELN, Colombia's second largest rebel force, blasted the pipeline four times last month taking the total to 35 times this year. Some 110,000 barrels of crude were spilled between January and June, generating a cost of more than $9.3 million in clean-up bills and the value of lost production.
The ELN, set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, specializes in attacks on oil infrastructure and is said to have mounted a series of cross-border raids in the last few months.
This has led the Venezuelan military to pursue suspected ELN rebels back into Colombian territory sparking a diplomatic row between the two countries' governments.
